sanskrit: dharmam eva prapadyante na hiṃsanti parasparam anugṛhṇanti cānyonyaṃ yadā rakṣati bhūmipaḥ
english: They take refuge in dharma alone, they do no violence to one another, and they show each other kindness—when the lord of the earth protects them.

sanskrit: yajante ca trayo varṇā mahāyajñaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ yuktāś cādhīyate śāstraṃ yadā rakṣati bhūmipaḥ
english: The three orders perform their great sacrifices, each in its own manner, and devoted men study the scriptures—when the lord of the earth protects them.

sanskrit: vārtāmūlo hy ayaṃ lokas trayyā vai dhāryate sadā tat sarvaṃ vartate samyag yadā rakṣati bhūmipaḥ
english: This world is rooted in livelihood and is forever upheld by the threefold Veda; all of this proceeds rightly when the lord of the earth protects it.

sanskrit: yadā rājā dhuraṃ śreṣṭhām ādāya vahati prajāḥ mahatā balayogena tadā lokaḥ prasīdati
english: When the king takes up the noblest yoke and bears his subjects forward with a great application of strength, then the world is at peace.

sanskrit: yasyābhāve ca bhūtānām abhāvaḥ syāt samantataḥ bhāve ca bhāvo nityaḥ syāt kas taṃ na pratipūjayet
english: In whose absence there would be the utter ruin of all beings, and in whose presence their continuance is ensured—who would not honor him?

sanskrit: tasya yo vahate bhāraṃ sarvalokasukhāvaham tiṣṭhet priyahite rājña ubhau lokau hi yo jayet
english: He who bears the burden of the king—a burden that brings happiness to all the world—and abides ever in his welfare and his pleasure, wins both worlds.

sanskrit: yas tasya puruṣaḥ pāpaṃ manasāpy anucintayet asaṃśayam iha kliṣṭaḥ pretyāpi narakaṃ patet
english: The man who plots evil against him even in thought will, beyond doubt, suffer affliction here, and after death fall into hell as well.

sanskrit: na hi jātv avamantavyo manuṣya iti bhūmipaḥ mahatī devatā hy eṣā nararūpeṇa tiṣṭhati
english: The lord of the earth must never be despised on the grounds that he is but a man, for this is a mighty deity standing here in human form.

sanskrit: kurute pañca rūpāṇi kālayuktāni yaḥ sadā bhavaty agnis tathādityo mṛtyur vaiśravaṇo yamaḥ
english: For he assumes, ever according to the occasion, five forms: he becomes Agni, and the Sun, and Death, and Vaiśravaṇa, and Yama.

sanskrit: yadā hy āsīd ataḥ pāpān dahaty ugreṇa tejasā mithyopacarito rājā tadā bhavati pāvakaḥ
english: For when the king, falsely served, burns up the wicked with fierce splendor, then he becomes Fire.

sanskrit: yadā paśyati cāreṇa sarvabhūtāni bhūmipaḥ kṣemaṃ ca kṛtvā vrajati tadā bhavati bhāskaraḥ
english: When the lord of the earth, through his spies, watches over all beings, and goes about securing their welfare, then he becomes the Sun.

sanskrit: aśucīṃś ca yadā kruddhaḥ kṣiṇoti śataśo narān saputrapautrān sāmātyāṃs tadā bhavati so 'ntakaḥ
english: And when in anger he destroys impure men by the hundred, together with their sons and grandsons and ministers, then he becomes the Ender.

sanskrit: yadā tv adhārmikān sarvāṃs tīkṣṇair daṇḍair niyacchati dhārmikāṃś cānugṛhṇāti bhavaty atha yamas tadā
english: But when he restrains all the unrighteous with sharp punishments and favors the righteous, then he becomes Yama.

sanskrit: yadā tu dhanadhārābhis tarpayaty upakāriṇaḥ ācchinatti ca ratnāni vividhāny apakāriṇām
english: And when he gratifies his benefactors with streams of wealth, and strips away the various treasures of those who do him harm—

sanskrit: śriyaṃ dadāti kasmai cit kasmāc cid apakarṣati tadā vaiśravaṇo rājaṃl loke bhavati bhūmipaḥ
english: when he bestows fortune upon one and withdraws it from another, then, O king, the lord of the earth becomes Vaiśravaṇa in the world.

sanskrit: nāsyāpavāde sthātavyaṃ dakṣeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā dharmyam ākāṅkṣatā lābham īśvarasyānasūyatā
english: One who is capable, untiring in his deeds, who seeks lawful gain and bears no grudge against his lord, must never stand in censure of him.

sanskrit: na hi rājñaḥ pratīpāni kurvan sukham avāpnuyāt putro bhrātā vayasyo vā yady apy ātmasamo bhavet
english: For no man who acts against the king can obtain happiness—be he son, or brother, or friend, even were he the king's own equal.

sanskrit: kuryāt kṛṣṇagatiḥ śeṣaṃ jvalito 'nilasārathiḥ na tu rājñābhipannasya śeṣaṃ kva cana vidyate
english: Fire whose course is black, blazing with the wind for its charioteer, may leave some remnant behind; but for the man whom the king has fallen upon, no remnant is found anywhere.

sanskrit: tasya sarvāṇi rakṣyāṇi dūrataḥ parivarjayet mṛtyor iva jugupseta rājasvaharaṇān naraḥ
english: All things that belong to the king and are under his protection a man should shun from afar; he should recoil from seizing the king's property as he would from death.

sanskrit: naśyed abhimṛśan sadyo mṛgaḥ kūṭam iva spṛśan ātmasvam iva saṃrakṣed rājasvam iha buddhimān
english: He who lays hands upon it perishes at once, like a deer that touches a snare; the wise man should guard the king's property here as if it were his own.

sanskrit: mahāntaṃ narakaṃ ghoram apratiṣṭham acetasaḥ patanti cirarātrāya rājavittāpahāriṇaḥ
english: Into a great and terrible hell, bottomless, the senseless men who steal the king's wealth fall, there to remain for many a long night.

sanskrit: rājā bhojo virāṭ samrāṭ kṣatriyo bhūpatir nṛpaḥ ya evaṃ stūyate śabdaiḥ kas taṃ nārcitum icchati
english: King, lord, sovereign, emperor, kṣatriya, master of the earth, ruler of men—he who is extolled by such titles, who would not wish to honor him?

sanskrit: tasmād bubhūṣur niyato jitātmā saṃyatendriyaḥ medhāvī smṛtimān dakṣaḥ saṃśrayeta mahīpatim
english: Therefore one who would prosper—disciplined, self-conquered, his senses restrained, intelligent, mindful, and capable—should take service with the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: kṛtajñaṃ prājñam akṣudraṃ dṛḍhabhaktiṃ jitendriyam dharmanityaṃ sthitaṃ sthityāṃ mantriṇaṃ pūjayen nṛpaḥ
english: The king should honor a counselor who is grateful, wise, generous of spirit, steadfast in devotion, master of his senses, ever firm in dharma, and constant in his proper conduct.

sanskrit: dṛḍhabhaktiṃ kṛtaprajñaṃ dharmajñaṃ saṃyatendriyam śūram akṣudrakarmāṇaṃ niṣiddhajanam āśrayet
english: He should rely upon a man of firm devotion, of seasoned wisdom, knowing dharma, his senses controlled, valiant, of no mean deeds, and free of any forbidden following.

sanskrit: rājā pragalbhaṃ puruṣaṃ karoti; rājā kṛśaṃ bṛṃhayate manuṣyam rājābhipannasya kutaḥ sukhāni; rājābhyupetaṃ sukhinaṃ karoti
english: The king makes a man bold; the king makes the feeble man thrive; whence can there be happiness for one upon whom the king has fallen? The king makes happy the man he favors.

sanskrit: rājā prajānāṃ hṛdayaṃ garīyo; gatiḥ pratiṣṭhā sukham uttamaṃ ca yam āśritā lokam imaṃ paraṃ ca; jayanti samyak puruṣā narendram
english: The king is the very heart of his people, weighty above all; their recourse, their foundation, and their highest happiness. Men who take refuge in the lord of men rightly conquer both this world and the next.

sanskrit: narādhipaś cāpy anuśiṣya medinīṃ; damena satyena ca sauhṛdena mahadbhir iṣṭvā kratubhir mahāyaśās; triviṣṭape sthānam upaiti satkṛtam
english: And the ruler of men too, having governed the earth with self-restraint, with truth, and with goodwill, and having worshipped with great sacrifices, attains in glory an honored place in heaven.

sanskrit: sa evam ukto guruṇā kausalyo rājasattamaḥ prayatnāt kṛtavān vīraḥ prajānāṃ paripālanam
english: Thus addressed by his teacher, that best of kings, the heroic Kausalya, with diligent effort carried out the protection of his subjects.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pārthivena viśeṣeṇa kiṃ kāryam avaśiṣyate kathaṃ rakṣyo janapadaḥ kathaṃ rakṣyāś ca śatravaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What further duty in particular remains for a king to perform? How is the realm to be protected, and how are enemies to be guarded against?

sanskrit: kathaṃ cāraṃ prayuñjīta varṇān viśvāsayet katham kathaṃ bhṛtyān kathaṃ dārān kathaṃ putrāṃś ca bhārata
english: How should he employ his spies, and how win the confidence of the orders? How should he deal with his servants, how with his wives, and how with his sons, O Bhārata?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rājavṛttaṃ mahārāja śṛṇuṣvāvahito 'khilam yat kāryaṃ pārthivenādau pārthivaprakṛtena vā
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear in full, O great king, with close attention, the conduct of a king—what must first be done by the ruler himself, or by one of a kingly nature.

sanskrit: ātmā jeyaḥ sadā rājñā tato jeyāś ca śatravaḥ ajitātmā narapatir vijayeta kathaṃ ripūn
english: The king must always conquer himself first, and only then his enemies; for how can a ruler of men who has not conquered himself vanquish his foes?

sanskrit: etāvān ātmavijayaḥ pañcavargavinigrahaḥ jitendriyo narapatir bādhituṃ śaknuyād arīn
english: Self-conquest amounts to just this: the mastery of the five-fold group of the senses. A ruler of men whose senses are subdued is able to crush his foes.

sanskrit: nyaseta gulmān durgeṣu saṃdhau ca kurunandana nagaropavane caiva purodyāneṣu caiva ha
english: He should post guard-companies in the fortresses and at the junctions, O delight of the Kurus, and in the groves about the city and in its parks as well.

sanskrit: saṃsthāneṣu ca sarveṣu pureṣu nagarasya ca madhye ca naraśārdūla tathā rājaniveśane
english: And in all the assembly-places and the market-towns, and in the heart of the city, O tiger among men, and likewise within the royal residence.

sanskrit: praṇidhīṃś ca tataḥ kuryāj jaḍāndhabadhirākṛtīn puṃsaḥ parīkṣitān prājñān kṣutpipāsātapakṣamān
english: Then he should appoint secret agents disguised as idiots, blind men, and deaf men—well-tested, shrewd persons able to endure hunger, thirst, and the heat of the sun.

sanskrit: amātyeṣu ca sarveṣu mitreṣu trividheṣu ca putreṣu ca mahārāja praṇidadhyāt samāhitaḥ
english: And with a steady mind, O great king, he should set such agents upon all his ministers, upon allies of the three kinds, and upon his own sons.

sanskrit: pure janapade caiva tathā sāmantarājasu yathā na vidyur anyonyaṃ praṇidheyās tathā hi te
english: In the city and in the countryside, and among the neighboring kings, the agents to be deployed should be so placed that they do not know one another.

sanskrit: cārāṃś ca vidyāt prahitān pareṇa bharatarṣabha āpaṇeṣu vihāreṣu samavāyeṣu bhikṣuṣu
english: And he should detect the spies sent in by the enemy, O bull of the Bharatas—in the marketplaces, in the pleasure-houses, in the gatherings, and among the mendicants;

sanskrit: ārāmeṣu tathodyāne paṇḍitānāṃ samāgame veśeṣu catvare caiva sabhāsv āvasatheṣu ca
english: in the gardens and the parks, in the assemblies of the learned, in the brothels and at the crossroads, in the council-halls and the rest-houses.

sanskrit: evaṃ vihanyāc cāreṇa paracāraṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ cāreṇa vihataṃ sarvaṃ hataṃ bhavati pāṇḍava
english: In this way the discerning king should foil the enemy's espionage with espionage of his own; for when the enemy's spies are foiled, all his designs are foiled, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: yadā tu hīnaṃ nṛpatir vidyād ātmānam ātmanā amātyaiḥ saha saṃmantrya kuryāt saṃdhiṃ balīyasā
english: But when a king perceives by his own judgment that he is the weaker, he should take counsel with his ministers and conclude a peace with the stronger power.

sanskrit: ajñāyamāno hīnatve kuryāt saṃdhiṃ pareṇa vai lipsur vā kaṃ cid evārthaṃ tvaramāṇo vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: While his weakness is still unknown, the discerning king should make peace with his adversary—whether because he is in haste, or because he seeks to gain some particular object.

sanskrit: guṇavanto mahotsāhā dharmajñāḥ sādhavaś ca ye saṃdadhīta nṛpas taiś ca rāṣṭraṃ dharmeṇa pālayan
english: With those who are virtuous, of great energy, knowing dharma, and upright, the king should ally himself, governing his kingdom by dharma.

sanskrit: ucchidyamānam ātmānaṃ jñātvā rājā mahāmatiḥ pūrvāpakāriṇo hanyāl lokadviṣṭāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: When the great-minded king perceives that he is being undone, he should strike down those who first did him injury and all who are hated by the people.

sanskrit: yo nopakartuṃ śaknoti nāpakartuṃ mahīpatiḥ aśakyarūpaś coddhartum upekṣyas tādṛśo bhavet
english: A ruler who can neither do good nor do harm, and who is in his nature impossible to overthrow—such a one is to be left to himself.

sanskrit: yātrāṃ yāyād avijñātam anākrandam anantaram vyāsaktaṃ ca pramattaṃ ca durbalaṃ ca vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: The discerning king should march upon an enemy who is unaware, who has no ally to call upon, who is without near support, who is preoccupied, negligent, and weak.

sanskrit: yātrām ājñāpayed vīraḥ kalyapuṣṭabalaḥ sukhī pūrvaṃ kṛtvā vidhānaṃ ca yātrāyāṃ nagare tathā
english: The hero, when his army is sound and well-nourished and he himself at ease, should order the campaign—but only after first making due provision both for the march and for the city.

sanskrit: na ca vaśyo bhaved asya nṛpo yady api vīryavān hīnaś ca balavīryābhyāṃ karśayaṃs taṃ parāvaset
english: And though some king be valiant, if he will not submit to him, then one inferior in strength and prowess should wear him down and so subdue him.

sanskrit: rāṣṭraṃ ca pīḍayet tasya śastrāgniviṣamūrchanaiḥ amātyavallabhānāṃ ca vivādāṃs tasya kārayet varjanīyaṃ sadā yuddhaṃ rājyakāmena dhīmatā
english: He should harass that king's realm with sword, fire, and stupefying poison, and should foment quarrels among his ministers and favorites; for open war must always be avoided by the wise man who covets dominion.

sanskrit: upāyais tribhir ādānam arthasyāha bṛhaspatiḥ sāntvenānupradānena bhedena ca narādhipa yam arthaṃ śaknuyāt prāptuṃ tena tuṣyed dhi paṇḍitaḥ
english: Bṛhaspati declares that the gaining of one's object is by three means: by conciliation, by gifts, and by sowing dissension, O ruler of men; and the wise man should rest content with whatever object he can secure thereby.

sanskrit: ādadīta baliṃ caiva prajābhyaḥ kurunandana ṣaḍbhāgam amitaprajñas tāsām evābhiguptaye
english: And the king of boundless wisdom should take a tax from his subjects, a sixth part, O delight of the Kurus—and that for their very protection.

sanskrit: daśadharmagatebhyo yad vasu bahv alpam eva ca tan nādadīta sahasā paurāṇāṃ rakṣaṇāya vai
english: Whatever wealth, great or small, belongs to those who follow the tenfold path of dharma, he should not seize precipitately—and this for the protection of his townsfolk.

sanskrit: yathā putrās tathā paurā draṣṭavyās te na saṃśayaḥ bhaktiś caiṣāṃ prakartavyā vyavahāre pradarśite
english: As one's sons, so are the townsfolk to be regarded—of this there is no doubt; and affection toward them is to be shown in the conduct of public affairs.

sanskrit: sutaṃ ca sthāpayed rājā prājñaṃ sarvārthadarśinam vyavahāreṣu satataṃ tatra rājyaṃ vyavasthitam
english: And the king should appoint a wise son, who discerns all matters, to oversee judicial affairs continually; for therein the kingdom rests secure.

sanskrit: ākare lavaṇe śulke tare nāgavane tathā nyased amātyān nṛpatiḥ svāptān vā puruṣān hitān
english: Over the mines, the salt-works, the customs-tolls, the ferries, and the elephant-forests, the king should set trusted ministers, or faithful men devoted to his welfare.

sanskrit: samyag daṇḍadharo nityaṃ rājā dharmam avāpnuyāt nṛpasya satataṃ daṇḍaḥ samyag dharme praśasyate
english: A king who ever wields the rod of punishment rightly attains dharma; the constant and rightful exercise of punishment is, for a king, commended as dharma itself.

sanskrit: vedavedāṅgavit prājñaḥ sutapasvī nṛpo bhavet dānaśīlaś ca satataṃ yajñaśīlaś ca bhārata
english: A king should be learned in the Vedas and their auxiliaries, wise, given to austerity, ever liberal in giving, and devoted to sacrifice, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ete guṇāḥ samastāḥ syur nṛpasya satataṃ sthirāḥ kriyālope tu nṛpateḥ kutaḥ svargaḥ kuto yaśaḥ
english: All these virtues should abide ever firm in a king; but if a king neglects his duties, whence comes heaven for him, and whence renown?

sanskrit: yadā tu pīḍito rājā bhaved rājñā balīyasā tridhā tv ākrandya mitrāṇi vidhānam upakalpayet
english: But when a king is hard pressed by a stronger king, he should call upon his allies of the three kinds and make his arrangements accordingly.

sanskrit: ghoṣān nyaseta mārgeṣu grāmān utthāpayed api praveśayec ca tān sarvāñ śākhānagarakeṣv api
english: He should post cowherd-stations along the roads, and even break up the outlying villages, and bring all their people within the suburbs and lesser towns.

sanskrit: ye guptāś caiva durgāś ca deśās teṣu praveśayet dhanino balamukhyāṃś ca sāntvayitvā punaḥ punaḥ
english: He should bring the wealthy folk and the leaders of his forces into those regions that are well-guarded and easily defended, soothing them again and again.

sanskrit: sasyābhihāraṃ kuryāc ca svayam eva narādhipaḥ asaṃbhave praveśasya dāhayed agninā bhṛśam
english: The ruler of men should himself gather in the standing crops; and where they cannot be brought in, he should have them thoroughly burned with fire.

sanskrit: kṣetrastheṣu ca sasyeṣu śatror upajapen narān vināśayed vā sarvasvaṃ balenātha svakena vai
english: As for crops still standing in the enemy's fields, he should suborn men to corrupt them, or else destroy the whole of his foe's substance with his own forces.

sanskrit: nadīṣu mārgeṣu sadā saṃkramān avasādayet jalaṃ nisrāvayet sarvam anisrāvyaṃ ca dūṣayet
english: On the rivers and along the roads he should always break down the bridges; he should drain off all the water, and what cannot be drained off he should foul.

sanskrit: tadātvenāyatībhiś ca vivadan bhūmyanantaram pratīghātaḥ parasyājau mitrakāle 'py upasthite
english: Whether disputing over the immediate moment or over the future, he must repel his neighboring foe in battle—even when the hour for an ally's aid has come.

sanskrit: durgāṇāṃ cābhito rājā mūlacchedaṃ prakārayet sarveṣāṃ kṣudravṛkṣāṇāṃ caityavṛkṣān vivarjayet
english: And all about the fortresses the king should have all the lesser trees cut down to their roots—but he should spare the sacred trees of the shrines.

sanskrit: pravṛddhānāṃ ca vṛkṣāṇāṃ śākhāḥ pracchedayet tathā caityānāṃ sarvathā varjyam api patrasya pātanam
english: Of the full-grown trees he should have the branches lopped off likewise; but of the sacred trees of the shrines, even the felling of a leaf is by all means to be avoided.

sanskrit: prakaṇṭhīḥ kārayet samyag ākāśajananīs tathā āpūrayec ca parikhāḥ sthāṇunakrajhaṣākulāḥ
english: He should have proper parapets constructed, and likewise openings that admit the sky; and he should fill the moats so that they teem with stakes, crocodiles, and great fish.

sanskrit: kaḍaṅgadvārakāṇi syur ucchvāsārthe purasya ha teṣāṃ ca dvāravad guptiḥ kāryā sarvātmanā bhavet
english: There should be small barred gateways for the city to breathe through; and these too must be guarded with all care, just like the main gates.

sanskrit: dvāreṣu ca gurūṇy eva yantrāṇi sthāpayet sadā āropayec chataghnīś ca svādhīnāni ca kārayet
english: At the gates he should ever set up massive engines, and should mount the śataghnīs, and keep them all under his own command.

sanskrit: kāṣṭhāni cābhihāryāṇi tathā kūpāṃś ca khānayet saṃśodhayet tathā kūpān kṛtān pūrvaṃ payorthibhiḥ
english: He should bring in stores of timber, and have wells dug; and he should also cleanse the wells made earlier by those in want of water.

sanskrit: tṛṇacchannāni veśmāni paṅkenāpi pralepayet nirharec ca tṛṇaṃ māse caitre vahnibhayāt puraḥ
english: Houses thatched with grass he should plaster over even with mud; and in the month of Caitra he should clear the grass out of the city for fear of fire.

sanskrit: naktam eva ca bhaktāni pācayeta narādhipaḥ na divāgnir jvaled gehe varjayitvāgnihotrikam
english: The ruler of men should have meals cooked only by night; by day no fire should burn in any house, save in that of the keeper of the sacred fire.

sanskrit: karmārāriṣṭaśālāsu jvaled agniḥ samāhitaḥ gṛhāṇi ca praviśyātha vidheyaḥ syād dhutāśanaḥ
english: In the smithies and the lying-in houses fire may burn, but kept under control; and when fire is brought into the dwellings, the flame must be held in check.

sanskrit: mahādaṇḍaś ca tasya syād yasyāgnir vai divā bhavet praghoṣayed athaivaṃ ca rakṣaṇārthaṃ purasya vai
english: And a heavy penalty should fall upon any man in whose house a fire is found by day; and this the king should proclaim aloud, for the safeguarding of the city.

sanskrit: bhikṣukāṃś cākrikāṃś caiva kṣībonmattān kuśīlavān bāhyān kuryān naraśreṣṭha doṣāya syur hi te 'nyathā
english: Beggars, wandering cart-folk, the drunk and the deranged, and strolling players he should keep outside, O best of men; for otherwise they prove a source of mischief.

sanskrit: catvareṣu ca tīrtheṣu sabhāsv āvasatheṣu ca yathārhavarṇaṃ praṇidhiṃ kuryāt sarvatra pārthivaḥ
english: At the crossroads, the bathing-places, the council-halls, and the rest-houses, the king should everywhere station an informant of a station suited to each place.

sanskrit: viśālān rājamārgāṃś ca kārayeta narādhipaḥ prapāś ca vipaṇīś caiva yathoddeśaṃ samādiśet
english: The ruler of men should have the royal highways made broad, and should ordain the watering-booths and the market-rows each according to its proper place.
